# Database Schema

**PostgreSQL on Supabase.** The executable definition is
[`supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql`](../supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql); this document explains it.
An earlier revision of this file proposed MongoDB with Mongoose; that was replaced in favour of a
relational schema, because the clinical, supply and billing records are heavily related and the
reporting questions (cover by ward, revenue by method, stock movement over time) are joins.

---

## Design rules

**Understandable identifiers, generated by the client.** Primary keys are `text` and come from the
application (`patient-3`, `med-adrenal-1`, `treat-0004`). Optimistic writes are then idempotent and the
client never has to reconcile an identifier, while uniqueness is still enforced by the primary key: a
collision is reported as `409 duplicate_id` and the client reloads. Human-readable sequences
(`MRN-2026-0004`, `INV-2026-0007`) come from the `counters` table.

**Child tables for repeated entities, JSONB for embedded value objects.** A prescription, an invoice
line, a payment transaction, a ward holding and an extracted report field are all rows in their own
table, because they are queried and aggregated independently. Something that is only ever read and
written with its parent — a patient's allergies, emergency contact and current admission, a supplier's
lead-time history, a drug's regional pressure — stays JSONB. The node registry in
`api/_lib/registry.ts` is the single declaration of which is which, and drives both directions of
mapping.

**snake_case in SQL, camelCase in the domain model.** The conversion is mechanical
(`currentAdmission` ↔ `current_admission`), so adding a field to a domain type and its migration is
enough to persist it. The handful of irregular mappings live in the registry.

**Derived values are never stored.** Risk scores, days of cover, redistribution proposals, alert
payloads, invoice totals and biomarker trends are recomputed from the stored rows by the engines in
`src/engine/`. Nothing computes a figure twice and disagrees with itself.

**Row level security on every table, with no permissive policy.** The browser uses the anon key for
credentials only; the API reads and writes with the service role, which bypasses RLS. An anon-key query
against any table therefore returns nothing. RLS is left unforced so the Supabase table editor can
still inspect rows.

---

## Entity relationships

```text
auth.users ──1:1── profiles ──┬── staff        (role in admin/doctor/nurse/receptionist/cashier)
                              └── patients     (role = patient)

patients ──┬── appointments ── staff (doctor)
           ├── treatments ──┬── prescriptions ── medicines
           │                └── medical_reports (linked_report_ids)
           ├── administrations
           ├── vitals
           ├── invoices ──┬── invoice_items
           │              └── payment_transactions
           └── medical_reports ── report_fields

medicines ──┬── ward_stock            (per-ward holdings and par levels)
            ├── prescriptions
            ├── transfer_proposals    (accepted/declined redistribution decisions)
            └── alerts                (acknowledged shortage alerts)

audit_log     append-only ledger, actors referenced by id
counters      human-readable ID sequences
```

## Tables

### Identity

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `staff` | `id`, `employee_id` unique, `email` unique, `role`, `department`, `shift`, `shift_start_hour` | workforce; `role` is constrained to the five staff roles |
| `profiles` | `id` → `auth.users`, `role`, `staff_id` → `staff`, `patient_id` → `patients` | the authorisation profile; a check constraint requires a staff link for staff roles and a patient link for the patient role |

### Patients and encounters

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `patients` | `id`, `mrn` unique, `name`, `dob`, `gender`, `allergies` jsonb, `emergency_contact` jsonb, `current_admission` jsonb, `chronic_conditions` text[], `resolved_conditions` text[] | indexed on `name`, `mrn`, `registered_at` |
| `appointments` | `id`, `patient_id`, `doctor_id`, `scheduled_for`, `status`, `acuity`, `triage_notes`, `queue_position` | statuses: scheduled, checked_in, in_consult, completed, cancelled, no_show |
| `treatments` | `id`, `patient_id`, `doctor_id`, `diagnosis`, `icd10_code`, `linked_report_ids` text[] | one consultation |
| `prescriptions` | `id`, `treatment_id` cascade, `medicine_id`, `frequency`, `duration_days`, `quantity`, `route`, `substitute_for`, `dispense_status`, `stock_advisory`, `ordinal` | a therapeutic substitution is recorded, not silently applied |
| `administrations` | `id`, `prescription_id`, `patient_id`, `scheduled_for`, `status`, `administered_at`, `administered_by`, `vitals_id` | the eMAR record; `administered_by` is written from the verified session |
| `vitals` | `id`, `patient_id`, `recorded_at`, temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, SpO2, pain score | indexed on `(patient_id, recorded_at desc)` |

### Formulary

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `medicines` | `id`, `sku` unique, `brand_name`, `generic_name`, `category`, `form`, `strength`, `unit_price`, `current_stock`, `allocated_stock`, `reorder_threshold`, `economic_order_quantity`, `safety_stock_days`, `consumption_history` int[], `regional_alert` jsonb, `supplier` jsonb, `therapeutic_alternatives` text[], `controlled_substance` | `consumption_history` is the daily dispense ledger, oldest first; it drives the EWMA burn rate |
| `ward_stock` | `(medicine_id, ward)` primary key, `quantity`, `par_level`, `ordinal` | the facility total is the sum of these rows, which is what makes an inter-ward transfer stock-neutral |

### Revenue

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `invoices` | `id`, `invoice_number` unique, `patient_id`, `cashier_id`, `tax_pct`, `payment_status` | status is a stored projection of the transaction ledger |
| `invoice_items` | `id`, `invoice_id` cascade, `item_type`, `description`, `quantity`, `unit_price`, `ordinal` | consultation, medication, procedure, diagnostic_report, room_charge |
| `payment_transactions` | `id`, `invoice_id` cascade, `payment_method`, `amount_paid`, `reference`, `processed_at`, `processed_by` | cash, credit_card, debit_card, upi, insurance_claim |

### Report simplifier

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `medical_reports` | `id`, `patient_id`, `uploaded_by`, `uploaded_by_role`, `file_name`, `file_mime_type`, `file_size_bytes`, `report_category`, `report_date`, `ocr_extraction_status`, `ocr_confidence`, `raw_ocr_text`, `medical_disclaimer`, `doctor_notes`, `archived`, `resolved_reason` | the original document bytes are deliberately not retained |
| `report_fields` | `id`, `report_id` cascade, `ordinal`, `test_name`, `normalized_key`, `value`, `value_text`, `unit`, `ref_min`, `ref_max`, `ref_text`, `ref_critical_low`, `ref_critical_high`, `status`, `plain_language_explanation`, `category`, `confidence`, `matched_alias` | `normalized_key` (fbs, hba1c, creatinine) is the join that builds longitudinal trends; the nested reference range is flattened into columns here and rebuilt by the registry |

### Supply decisions and governance

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `transfer_proposals` | `id`, `medicine_id`, `from_ward`, `to_ward`, `quantity`, `surplus_at_source`, `deficit_at_target`, `rationale`, `estimated_sps_drop`, `wards_recovered`, `status`, `decided_at`, `decided_by` | live proposals are derived, not stored; this is the decision ledger |
| `alerts` | `id`, `medicine_id`, `drug_name`, `tier`, `sps`, `message`, `created_at`, `acknowledged`, `acknowledged_by`, `acknowledged_at` | written when an alert is acknowledged |
| `audit_log` | `id`, `at`, `actor_id`, `actor_name`, `actor_role`, `action`, `target`, `detail` | append-only; indexed on `at`, `actor_id` and `action`. The actor comes from the verified session, never from the request body |
| `counters` | `key`, `value` | backs `MRN-2026-0007`-style identifiers |

---

## Applying changes

Add a new migration file, `supabase/migrations/0002_<description>.sql`, and apply it with the Supabase
CLI or the SQL editor. Never edit `0001_init.sql` after it has been applied anywhere: it is the record
of what the deployed database already is.
